description.narrative:
In Mali, the impact of climate change has been heavily felt over the past 40 years with increased rates of desertification and flooding and serious consequences on food security (availability and accessibility of food, etc.). The rural women in Mali are feeling the effects of climate change in their daily lives. They find that once-reliable crops no longer grow or that the frequency of rains destroys their ability to earn a living, and with less access to resources than men, they find it harder to bounceback. Yet they know what needs to be done to help their households and communities adapt to climate change and build resilience. In addition to this, other challenges that affect their capacity include lack of access to credit, water and storage infrastructure, equipment and tools,and agricultural inputs such as organic fertilizers.
The project Soro Kera is in the Segou Region in Mali, specifically in the Baraouéli Circle and implemented with Oxfam’s local partner, the Association des Femmes Pasteuresde Baraouéli (AFPB). AFPB’s members have benefited from support with other projects (2 larger Danish/Belgium cooperation projects) in terms of savings mobilization, training for market gardening activities as well as local milk production. With the support of Oxfam, women have benefited from seeds andmarket gardening tools, but also from literacy sessions and training in farming techniques. Since then, they feel more autonomous, thanks to the income from market gardening products. To reinforce and sustain this support, the project intends the develop 2 community market gardening perimeters and the construction of a resource <(>&<)> service centre containing a storage warehouse that will benefit women and more broadly the community of the same area.
This project aims to support the rural women in Baraouéli to further professionalize and succeed in agribusiness by equipping them and strengthening access to essential and innovative infrastructure. It specifically invests in the development of a 7-hectareplot of land which includes a market garden perimeter and its fencing; the installation of watering basins; the installation of solar wells and drip systems on the plot, where they grow shallots, onions, pepper, potatoes, lettuce, cucumbers, and eggplant. The project supports the construction of a storage warehouse including a sales kiosk, a training room and heavy equipment (solar panel and refrigerated room). The project will ensure the purchase of small equipment and inputs, the facilitation of trainingand the implementation of visibility tools such as success stories.

participating-org.narrative: Oxfam Novib was founded in 1956 as the Netherlands Organisation for International Assistance (Novib), and joined forces with Oxfam in 1994. Oxfam Novib is member of the Oxfam International confederation. Working together in the confederation, the Oxfam affiliates can speak with one clear and compelling voice on issues of global concern: climate change, health and education for all, agriculture, trade, and conflicts and emergencies. Oxfam Novib's main office is based in The Netherlands, it supports the work of a network of local offices, the implementation of global projects, fundraising, campaigning and advocacy. Oxfam Novib’s the Hague office contributes towards this project’s implementation.
